name: Firebase
description: Firebase is Google's application development platform for building and operating web and mobile apps.
agentUseSummary: Connect one exact Firebase Project through Relay's confidential Google OAuth client with only firebase.readonly and offline access, then let agents list a bounded page of active Projects, inspect the exact selected Project, and list bounded App summaries. Relay V1 excludes API-key identifiers and values, app configs, credentials, product data, writes, administration, raw APIs, broader Google scopes, and pagination.

credentialRequirements.helpText: Relay-owned confidential Google OAuth client ID configured only on Railway.

capabilities.label: Read Firebase Projects
capabilities.description: List a bounded page of accessible Projects and inspect one exact selected Project.

capabilities.label: Read selected-Project Apps
capabilities.description: List a bounded App summary without API-key identifiers or configuration.

approvalRequired.label: List Firebase Projects
approvalRequired.description: List at most twenty-five active Firebase Projects from the first page accessible to the OAuth grant.

approvalRequired.label: Read selected Project
approvalRequired.description: Read one exact selected Firebase Project and verify its resource binding.

approvalRequired.label: List selected-Project Apps
approvalRequired.description: List at most twenty-five active Apps from the selected Project's first search page without API-key identifiers or app configs.

blocked.label: Change Firebase
blocked.description: Project and App creation, update, provisioning, deletion, undelete, and every product mutation are outside V1.

blocked.label: Read sensitive Firebase data
blocked.description: API-key identifiers and values, SDK/app configs, credentials, service accounts, user data, databases, storage, logs, analytics, messaging, and product-specific data are outside V1.

blocked.label: Administer Firebase
blocked.description: IAM, users, billing, OAuth clients, service accounts, extensions, App Check, security rules, and administration are outside V1.

blocked.label: Use raw Firebase or Google APIs
blocked.description: Arbitrary REST, paths, queries, page tokens, pagination, Cloud Platform scopes, product APIs, Admin SDK, CLI tokens, and raw responses are outside V1.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: All three bounded Firebase reads require matching approval.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: All three selected read-only tools run without Relay per-action approval while exact Project binding, fixed requests, bounds, redaction, audit, refresh, and provider limits remain enforced.

runtimeSupport.description: Relay mounts three fixed Firebase Management API read wrappers and attaches refreshed OAuth access tokens server-side.
Relay mounts three fixed Firebase Management API read wrappers and attaches refreshed OAuth access tokens server-side.

providerSetup.blocker: Relay's confidential Google OAuth application, exact Railway callback, firebase.readonly consent configuration, Firebase Management API enablement, and staging credentials require provider-console completion and authorized staging acceptance.
providerSetup.nextAction: Configure the confidential Google OAuth web client with Relay's exact Railway callback and firebase.readonly, enable the Firebase Management API, add staging credentials, then validate exact scope, offline refresh, revoke, selected-Project binding, denial, and all three bounded reads.

evidence.supports: Firebase documents active Project listing at GET /v1beta1/projects, bounded pageSize, short-lived page tokens, and firebase.readonly as an accepted authorization scope.
Firebase documents consistent exact Project reads at GET /v1beta1/projects/{projectId} with firebase.readonly.

Firebase documents searchApps as the cross-platform App-summary selector surface, with pageSize, active-only filtering, and FirebaseAppInfo fields including API-key identifiers that Relay explicitly redacts.
Google documents the confidential web-server authorization-code flow, CSRF state, offline access, prompt=consent refresh-token behavior, token refresh, and HTTPS authorization and token endpoints.
Google documents provider-side OAuth grant revocation through oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke.
